title: Programmable banking platform Hyperlayer  raises £19.5m
summary: Hyperlayer, the London-based fintech founded by former Morgan Stanley executives to help banks modernise without replacing their core systems, has raised £19.5 million at a £195 million valuation.
content: London-based programmable banking platform Hyperlayer has successfully raised £19.5 million in a new funding round, achieving a £195 million valuation. Founded by former Morgan Stanley executives, the fintech startup aims to help traditional banks modernise their technology infrastructure without the need to completely replace their existing core banking systems.
content_ta: London-ஜ merkezant programmable banking platform ஆன Hyperlayer புதிய நிதி திரட்டல் சுற்றில் £19.5 மில்லியன் திரட்டியுள்ளது, இதன் மூலம் இதன் மதிப்பு £195 மில்லியனாக உயர்ந்துள்ளது. முன்னாள் Morgan Stanley அதிகாரிகளால் தொடங்கப்பட்ட இந்த fintech நிறுவனம், பாரம்பரிய வங்கிகள் தங்கள் core systems-ஐ முழுமையாக மாற்றாமல் தங்கள் technology infrastructure-ஐ modernise செய்ய உதவுகிறது.

title: Starling build agentic fincrime investigator that takes 17 seconds
summary: Starling has deployed an agentic "financial crime investigator" that the UK digital bank says can carry out an end-to-end investigation within 17 seconds.
content: UK digital bank Starling has deployed a new agentic financial crime investigator designed to streamline security processes. According to the bank, the automated system is capable of carrying out a complete end-to-end investigation in just 17 seconds, significantly improving the speed and efficiency of detecting and reviewing suspicious financial activities.
content_ta: UK டிஜிட்டல் வங்கியான Starling, பாதுகாப்பு செயல்முறைகளை விரைவுபடுத்தும் நோக்கில் புதிய ஏஜென்டிக் 'financial crime investigator'-ஐ அறிமுகப்படுத்தியுள்ளது. சந்தேகத்திற்கிடமான நிதி நடவடிக்கைகளைக் கண்டறிந்து முழுமையான விசாரணையை வெறும் 17 வினாடிகளுக்குள் முடிக்க இந்த தானியங்கி அமைப்பு உதவும் என்று வங்கி தெரிவித்துள்ளது.

title: Kraken’s $80 stablecoin fee gap exposes hidden costs
summary:

Understand the crypto stories that matter and what to watch next. Get The Catalyst in your inbox

He emphasizes that while AI holds immense power to revolutionize entrepreneurship, the current market is facing heavy financial scrutiny and a growing demand for tangible investment returns.
content_ta: செயற்கை நுண்ணறிவுத்துறை கிட்டத்தட்ட உறுதியாக ஒரு நிதி சொத்து குமிழியை சந்தித்து வருவதாக Ken Griffin தெரிவித்துள்ளார். இந்த மதிப்பீட்டிற்குப் பிறகும், தொழில்நுட்பத்தின் மாற்றத்தை உருவாக்கும் திறனில் அவர் உறுதியான நம்பிக்கை கொண்டுள்ளார். AI ஆனது தொழில்முனைவோரை புரட்சிகரமாக்க பெரும் ஆற்றலைக் கொண்டிருந்தாலும், தற்போதைய சந்தையானது கடுமையான நிதி ஆய்வையும் உறுதியான முதலீட்டு லாபத்திற்கான தேவையையும் எதிர்கொண்டுள்ளதாக அவர் வலியுறுத்துகிறார்.

title: BlackRock Submits SEC Filing for Bitcoin ETF Designed for Partial Downside Buffer Alongside Capped Upside
summary: On October 19, 2026, iShares Trust, advised by BlackRock Fund Advisors, filed a post-effective amendment to its registration statement with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) for a proposed new series named the iShares Bitcoin Managed Protection ETF, intended to trade under the ticker... Read More
content: On October 19, 2026, iShares Trust, advised by BlackRock Fund Advisors, submitted an SEC filing for a proposed Bitcoin ETF. The new fund, named the iShares Bitcoin Managed Protection ETF, is designed to offer partial downside protection while also limiting the potential upside for investors.
content_ta: அக்டோபர் 19, 2026 அன்று, BlackRock Fund Advisors நிறுவனத்தின் ஆலோசனையின்படி iShares Trust, ஒரு புதிய Bitcoin ETF-க்கான SEC ஆவணங்களை சமர்ப்பித்தது. iShares Bitcoin Managed Protection ETF என பெயரிடப்பட்டுள்ள இந்த புதிய நிதி, முதலீட்டாளர்களுக்கு ஓரளவு சரிவிலிருந்து பாதுகாப்பையும் அதே நேரத்தில் லாப வரம்பைக் கட்டுப்படுத்தும் வகையிலும் வடிவமைக்கப்பட்டுள்ளது.

title: MoonPay, Upbit parent Dunamu explore collaboration on stablecoin payments, GIWA expansion
summary: The companies also plan to explore ways to broaden global access to Dunamu's Ethereum Layer 2, GIWA chain.
content: MoonPay and Dunamu, the parent company of Upbit, are exploring a new collaboration focused on stablecoin payments and the expansion of the GIWA chain. As part of this initiative, the companies also plan to investigate methods for broadening global access to Dunamu's Ethereum Layer 2 network.
content_ta: MoonPay மற்றும் Upbit-இன் தாய் நிறுவனமான Dunamu ஆகியவை stablecoin கொடுப்பனவுகள் மற்றும் GIWA செயின் விரிவாக்கம் குறித்து புதிய கூட்டாண்மையை ஆராய்ந்து வருகின்றன. இந்த முயற்சியின் ஒரு பகுதியாக, Dunamu-வின் Ethereum Layer 2 நெட்வொர்க்கிற்கான உலகளாவிய அணுகலை விரிவுபடுத்துவதற்கான வழிகளையும் இந்நிறுவனங்கள் ஆராய திட்டமிட்டுள்ளன.

title: Kazakhstan shuts down mobile access to 6 major crypto exchanges
summary:
September orders bind Apple and Google upon service and target unauthorized services in the AIFC; implementation remains unconfirmed.
Read the full story on CryptoSlate
Understand the crypto stories that matter and what to watch next. Get The Catalyst in your inbox
content: Kazakhstan has reportedly shut down mobile access to six major cryptocurrency exchanges. Government orders issued in September directed Apple and Google to restrict these unauthorized services operating within the Astana International Financial Centre, though full implementation of the blocks remains unconfirmed.
content_ta: கஜகஸ்தான் நாட்டில் ஆறு முக்கிய crypto exchanges தளங்களுக்கான மொபைல் இணைய அணுகல் துண்டிக்கப்பட்டுள்ளதாகத் தகவல்கள் வெளியாகியுள்ளன. செப்டம்பர் மாதம் பிறப்பிக்கப்பட்ட உத்தரவுகளின்படி, AIFC-க்குள் அனுமதியின்றி இயங்கும் சேவைகளைக் கட்டுப்படுத்துமாறு Apple மற்றும் Google நிறுவனங்களுக்கு அறிவுறுத்தப்பட்டுள்ளது. எனினும், இந்தத் தடை முழுமையாக அமல்படுத்தப்பட்டது குறித்த உறுதிப்படுத்தப்பட்ட தகவல்கள் இன்னும் வெளியாகவில்லை.

title: AI Is Splitting Software Into Winners and Losers, Citi’s Tyler Radke Says
summary:
Citi's Tyler Radke says AI is creating software winners and losers, as Salesforce agrees to buy Braze for $47.50 a share.
The post AI Is Splitting Software Into Winners and Losers, Citi’s Tyler Radke Says appeared first on BeInCrypto.
content: Artificial intelligence is creating a distinct divide between winners and losers in the software industry, according to Citi analyst Tyler Radke. This shift comes as industry developments continue to accelerate. Meanwhile, Salesforce has agreed to acquire Braze for $47.50 per share, marking a significant move in the evolving market landscape as companies adapt to new technological demands and competitive pressures brought on by AI advancements.
content_ta: Citi-ன் அனலிஸ்ட் Tyler Radke கூற்றுப்படி, AI தொழில்நுட்பம் மென்பொருள் துறையில் வெற்றியாளர்கள் மற்றும் தோற்பவர்களை தெளிவாக பிரித்து வருகிறது. இந்த சூழலில், Salesforce நிறுவனம் Braze-ஐ ஒரு பங்கிற்கு $47.50 விலையில் வாங்க ஒப்பந்தம் செய்துள்ளது. AI வளர்ச்சியால் ஏற்படும் புதிய தொழில்நுட்ப தேவைகளுக்கு ஏற்ப நிறுவனங்கள் தங்களை தகவமைத்துக் கொள்ளும் வேளையில், சந்தை நிலவரத்தில் இந்த ஒப்பந்தம் ஒரு முக்கிய நகர்வாக பார்க்கப்படுகிறது.

title: KOSPI Jumps 3.54%, Nikkei Gains 1.43%, But How Is Oil Driving the Rebound?
summary:
KOSPI and Nikkei rebound as oil prices ease, but Brent fell just 0.69% and stays above $100. Can the chip rally last?
The post KOSPI Jumps 3.54%, Nikkei Gains 1.43%, But How Is Oil Driving the Rebound? appeared first on BeInCrypto.
content: Asian markets experienced a strong rebound, with the KOSPI index jumping 3.54% and the Nikkei gaining 1.43%. This market recovery was driven by easing oil prices, although Brent crude fell only 0.69% and remained above the 100 dollar mark. Investors are now questioning whether the ongoing semiconductor rally can be sustained amidst these fluctuating energy market conditions.
content_ta: ஆசிய சந்தைகள் குறிப்பிடத்தக்க மீட்சியை சந்தித்துள்ளன, இதில் KOSPI குறியீடு 3.54% உயர்ந்தது மற்றும் Nikkei 1.43% லாபம் ஈட்டியது. எண்ணெய் விலை குறைந்ததே இந்த சந்தை மீட்சிக்கு காரணமாக இருந்தது, எனினும் Brent க்ரூட் 0.69% மட்டுமே சரிந்து 100 டாலருக்கு மேல் உள்ளது. இந்த நிலையற்ற எரிசக்தி சந்தை சூழலில், தற்போதைய சிப் (chip) எழுச்சி தொடருமா என்ற கேள்வி முதலீட்டாளர்கள் மத்தியில் எழுந்துள்ளது.

title: SpaceX guides $33 billion to $37 billion Q1 2027 revenue as AI compute takes over
summary:
SpaceX's pivot to AI compute signals a transformative shift in its business model, emphasizing the growing importance of AI infrastructure.
The post SpaceX guides $33 billion to $37 billion Q1 2027 revenue as AI compute takes over appeared first on Crypto Briefing.
content: SpaceX has projected a strong revenue between $33 billion and $37 billion for the first quarter of 2027. This financial outlook highlights a major business shift as artificial intelligence compute increasingly drives the company's operations and emphasizes the expanding role of advanced AI infrastructure in its future growth.
content_ta: 2027-ம் ஆண்டின் முதல் காலாண்டில் SpaceX நிறுவனம் 33 பில்லியன் டலர் முதல் 37 பில்லியன் டலர் வரை வருவாய் ஈட்டக்கூடும் என்று கணித்துள்ளது. நிறுவனத்தின் வணிக முறையில் ஏஐ கம்ப்யூட் முக்கிய பங்கு வகிக்கும் நிலையில் இந்த நிதி எதிர்பார்ப்பு வெளியாகியுள்ளது.

title: Nvidia spends a record nearly $2.2 million on federal lobbying in Q3
summary:
Nvidia's record lobbying spend highlights the critical role of regulatory influence in shaping the future of AI and semiconductor markets.
The post Nvidia spends a record nearly $2.2 million on federal lobbying in Q3 appeared first on Crypto Briefing.
content: Nvidia has spent a record nearly $2.2 million on federal lobbying during the third quarter. This significant investment in lobbying highlights the crucial role of regulatory influence and government relations in shaping the future development of artificial intelligence and semiconductor markets.
content_ta: மூன்றாவது காலாச்சிறில் Nvidia நிறுவனம் ஃபெடரல் லாபிங் செய்வதற்காக சாதனை அளவாக கிட்டத்தட்ட $2.2 மில்லியன் செலவிட்டுள்ளது. லாபிங்கில் செய்யப்பட்டுள்ள இந்த குறிப்பிடத்தக்க முதலீடு, செயற்கை நுண்ணறிவு மற்றும் செமிகண்டக்டர் சந்தைகளின் எதிர்காலத்தை வடிவமைப்பதில் ஒழுங்குமுறை தாக்கத்தின் முக்கிய பங்கை எடுத்துக்காட்டுகிறது.

title: S&P 500’s 15 largest stocks now hold a record 46.7% of the index
summary:
The concentration of market value in a few tech giants heightens volatility risk, making the S&P 500 more susceptible to sector-specific downturns.
The post S&P 500’s 15 largest stocks now hold a record 46.7% of the index appeared first on Crypto Briefing.
content: The 15 largest stocks in the S&P 500 have reached a record-breaking 46.7% share of the index's total market value. This high concentration of wealth in a handful of major companies significantly increases volatility risk, leaving the S&P 500 much more vulnerable to sector-specific market downturns.
content_ta: S&P 500 இன் மிகப்பெரிய 15 பங்குகள் குறியீட்டின் மொத்த சந்தை மதிப்பில் சாதனை அளவாக 46.7% ஐ எட்டியுள்ளன. இந்த அதிகப்படியான சந்தை மதிப்பு செறிவு நிலையற்ற தன்மையை அதிகரித்து, S&P 500 குறியீட்டை துறை சார்ந்த வீழ்ச்சிகளுக்கு அதிக அளவில் ஆளாக்குகிறது.

title: Ripple brings Wall Street into 24/7 stock bets, but HSBC warns markets are still thin
summary: Institutions can trade through Ripple Prime and post RLUSD as collateral. Finding enough buyers and sellers for large positions could prove harder.
content: Ripple is introducing institutional clients to around-the-clock stock trading through Ripple Prime, allowing them to use RLUSD as collateral. However, banking giant HSBC has issued a warning that market liquidity during these sessions remains thin, suggesting that executing large trades with sufficient buyers and sellers could present challenges.
content_ta: Ripple நிறுவனம் institutional வாடிக்கையாளர்களுக்கு Ripple Prime மூலம் 24 மணி நேர stock வர்த்தகத்தை அறிமுகப்படுத்துகிறது, மேலும் அவர்கள் RLUSD-ஐ collateral-ஆக பயன்படுத்த அனுமதிக்கிறது. இருப்பினும், HSBC வங்கி இதுபோன்ற நேரங்களில் market liquidity குறைவாகவே இருப்பதாக எச்சரித்துள்ளது, இதனால் பெரிய அளவிலான trade-களை செய்வதில் சவால்கள் இருக்கலாம்.

title: Solana’s Alpenglow, its biggest network overhaul since 2020, goes live Wednesday
summary: Alpenglow will replace the voting system Solana has used since 2020, targeting roughly 150-millisecond finality after months of testing that included a failed migration and rollback.
content: Solana is launching Alpenglow on Wednesday, marking its biggest network overhaul since 2020. The major upgrade replaces the network's long-standing voting system. It follows months of testing, which included a previous failed migration and subsequent rollback, and targets a finality time of roughly 150 milliseconds.
content_ta: 2020-க்குப் பிறகு Solana-வின் மிகப்பெரிய நெட்வொர்க் மேம்படுத்தலான Alpenglow புதன்கிழமை செயல்பாட்டுக்கு வருகிறது. இந்த முக்கிய மேம்படுத்தல், 2020 முதல் நெட்வொர்க் பயன்படுத்தி வந்த ஓட்டுப்பதிவு முறையை மாற்றுகிறது. தோல்வியடைந்த இடம்பெயர்வு மற்றும் ரோல்பேக் உள்ளிட்ட பல மாத பரிசோதனைகளுக்குப் பிறகு இது வருகிறது.

title: A company that vouches for websites had secret keys so weak that 8 of them were cracked
summary: Eight secret keys at eMudhra, an Indian firm that vouches for websites, were compromised. Browsers and software makers are rushing out fixes.
content: Eight secret keys at eMudhra, an Indian firm that vouches for websites, were compromised due to weak security. This security flaw allowed the keys to be cracked, posing potential risks to digital trust. In response to the breach, web browsers and software makers are currently rushing out emergency fixes to protect users and maintain secure online communications.
content_ta: வெப்பசைட்டுகளுக்கு உத்தரவாதம் அளிக்கும் இந்திய நிறுவனமான eMudhra-ன் எட்டு ரகசிய சாவிகள் பலவீனமான பாதுகாப்பு காரணமாக சமரசம் செய்யப்பட்டன. இந்த பாதுகாப்பு குறைபாடு சாவிகள் உடைக்கப்படுவதற்கு வழிவகுத்தது, இது டிஜிட்டல் நம்பிக்கைக்கு சாத்தியமான ஆபத்துகளை ஏற்படுத்துகிறது. இந்த மீறலுக்கு பதிலளிக்கும் விதமாக, பயனர்களைப் பாதுகாக்கவும் பாதுகாப்பான ஆன்லைன் தொடர்புகளைப் பேணவும் வலை உலாவி மற்றும் மென்பொருள் உருவாக்குநர்கள் அவசரகால திருத்தங்களை அவசரமாக வெளியிட்டு வருகின்றனர்.

title: Bitcoin hovers around $83,000 as AI earnings revive tech, ZEC jumps 11%
summary: Strong results from SpaceX and Super Micro sent Asian chip stocks surging, and ZEC led crypto higher after developers set a date for its next network upgrade.
content: Bitcoin hovered around $83,000 as strong earnings from major technology firms boosted sentiment across global markets. Asian chip stocks surged following positive results from SpaceX and Super Micro. Meanwhile, ZEC led cryptocurrency gains, jumping 11% after developers announced the scheduled date for its upcoming network upgrade.
content_ta: Bitcoin விலை $83,000 அருகில் வர்த்தகமானது. முன்னணி தொழில்நுட்ப நிறுவனங்களின் வலுவான வருவாய் உலகளாவிய சந்தைகளில் முதலீட்டாளர்களின் நம்பிக்கையை உயர்த்தியது. SpaceX மற்றும் Super Micro நிறுவனங்களின் சாதகமான முடிவுகளைத் தொடர்ந்து ஆசிய சிப் பங்குகளின் மதிப்பு உயர்ந்தது. இதற்கிடையில், அடுத்த நெட்வொர்க் மேம்படுத்தலுக்கான தேதியை டெவலப்பர்கள் அறிவித்ததை அடுத்து ZEC கிரிப்டோகரன்சி 11% உயர்ந்துள்ளது.

title: Tech giants rush to block 8 eMudhra certs that could enable fake sites
summary: A private key generation flaw allowed anyone to guess them and forge HTTPS certificates for any website.
content: Major tech giants are moving quickly to block eight eMudhra certificates following the discovery of a private key generation flaw. The vulnerability allowed unauthorized individuals to guess keys and potentially forge secure HTTPS certificates for any website, posing significant security risks. Companies are taking urgent measures to revoke trust in these compromised certificates to protect users from fake sites.

title: LemFi Launches Its Biggest Product Expansion Yet Alongside a New Global Brand, ‘Ambition Has No Passport’
summary:
LemFi, the financial platform for people building lives across borders, today announced the launch of its new global brand platform, “Ambition has no passport”, alongside a completely rebuilt app, launching the largest product expansion in its history.
More than two million customers use LemFi to move money to more than 30 countries, with over $2 billion in monthly transaction volume, and the company plans to add more countries next year. The expanded platform now includes savings and credit in the UK, eSIMs in more than 100 destinations, alongside LemFi’s existing international payments service.
People who move countries arrive with a career, a qualification and a savings record, only to find that almost none of it counts. A credit history rarely survives a border crossing. Around 304 million people now live outside the country where they were born, sending some $905 billion home each year. Yet many financial services remain designed around individual products or customers living their financial lives in a single country. LemFi is building its platform around that gap, extending from the international transfers on which the company was founded into a wider range of financial services designed for people whose lives span borders.
“We started LemFi because sending money home was broken. What we learned is that the harder problem starts after the transfer,” said Ridwan Olalere, co-founder and CEO of LemFi. “Our customers are building careers and businesses in one country while supporting people in another, and the financial system treats them as if they can only exist in one place at a time. That is the wrong answer for people this ambitious, so we have rebuilt LemFi to work the way their lives do. Ambition travels. The infrastructure behind it should travel too.”
Inside LemFi’s expanded platform
Transfers, still at the heart of it. Send money to more than 30 countries across Africa, Asia, Europe and beyond, from the same account that now saves, borrows and connects.
Savings that stay within reach in the UK. The LemFi Instant Access Savings Account currently pays a boosted 5% AER for the first six months from account opening; it then reverts to 3.04% AER (tracker), tracking the Bank of England base rate. Accounts open from £1, with no penalty for withdrawals. Deposits are held by ClearBank and protected by the Financial Services Compensation Scheme (FSCS) up to £120,000 per eligible depositor.
A credit history that travels in the UK. A revolving credit line, available subject to availability, is issued by Lemfi Credit through Pillar, the FCA-regulated credit provider LemFi acquired in 2025. It is available as a virtual card through Apple Pay and Google Pay and can be used for both spending and sending. Eligible customers can also see their Equifax credit score in the app for free.
eSIM in more than 100 destinations, in every market. Buy mobile data before arriving, with no SIM swap and no roaming bill.
A brand and an app rebuilt together
The app has been re-architected from the ground up to hold several products across several countries in a single account, rather than bolting them onto a transfer app. The redesign also brings LemFi’s products to the forefront of the experience, making them easier to discover and creating an architecture that lets the company add new services as it expands.
The company has also introduced its new global brand platform, “Ambition has no passport”, reflecting its focus on customers building careers, businesses, families and financial lives across borders. The new identity spans LemFi’s product interface, website, marketing and social channels and will roll out across its global markets.
“LemFi started as a way to send money home. Our customers turned it into a way to build a life across borders,” said Isabel Ron-Pedrique, VP of Design and Brand at LemFi. “They are not defined by the country they left. They are defined by what they are building. Ambition has no passport is not a line we placed on top of the product. It is the idea the whole system is built from, from the app you open in the morning to the poster you walk past on the way to work. We have built this brand to keep up with them”

title: Building on Strong Operational Foundations, N26 Appoints Michael Steen as Chief Communications Officer Ahead of Next Phase of Growth
summary:
N26 is refocusing on its next phase of growth and maturity: scaling the digital bank’s core markets of Germany, France, Italy and Spain to reinforce its leadership in European digital banking.
Six months into Mike Dargan’s tenure as CEO, with strengthened compliance and governance frameworks and a newly established management team in place, N26 will further sharpen its focus on Europe, rolling out a targeted product roadmap to drive customer relevance and primary account growth, starting with the launch of its new signature banking experience, N26 Aura, next month.
As part of this plan to drive execution, N26 has appointed Michael Steen as Chief Communications Officer (CCO) effective 1 January 2027. Michael brings extensive experience from Deutsche Bank, where he held the role of Managing Director and Head of External Communications and Newsroom. Prior to that, Michael served in a senior communications position at the European Central Bank. He began his career as a financial journalist for Reuters and the Financial Times.
In his role, he will work closely with the management team, in building relevance, resonance and trust among customers as the bank accelerates towards its ambition to be Europe’s Most Trusted Digital Primary Bank. With the appointment of Michael, alongside recently appointed Chief Financial Officer Marc Hess, N26 has taken significant steps in reshaping its management team to start the next chapter.
Mike Dargan, Chief Executive Officer of N26, said, “Building solid regulatory foundations, robust systems and trust at the core of how we operate has been a priority for me since joining N26. With these pillars firmly established, N26 is now well-positioned to accelerate towards our ambitions and deepen our relationships with more customers across Europe as their primary bank.”






Michael Steen, incoming Chief Communications Officer of N26, added, “N26 has redefined modern banking for millions of European consumers. As the company enters this next phase of scale and institutional maturity, transparent communication and strong stakeholder trust must come hand-in-hand with growth. I look forward to working alongside Mike and our management team as we continue to build Europe’s Most Trusted Digital Primary Bank.”

title: BRAC Bank Enhances Trade Finance Operations With Finastra
summary:
Finastra, a global leader in financial services software, today announced that BRAC Bank, one of Bangladesh's leading private commercial banks, has gone live with Finastra's Trade Innovation and Corporate Channels, and Conpend’s Trade AI solutions, creating a more connected trade finance environment for the bank and its corporate customers.
As trade volumes grow and customer expectations continue to evolve, BRAC Bank sought to modernize its trade finance operations, improve efficiency, and establish a scalable foundation for future growth. By replacing fragmented processes with an integrated digital platform, the bank is streamlining trade finance workflows – increasing straight-through processing and enhancing visibility across the trade finance lifecycle.
Building a Scalable, Future-Ready Trade Finance Platform
The new platform provides BRAC Bank with an integrated foundation for modern trade finance operations – delivering benefits across efficiency, customer engagement, and long-term scalability.
• Extensive digital trade capabilities: Enables streamlined trade finance operations with greater straight-through processing, improved efficiency, faster deployment of new services, while supporting compliance with evolving industry standards, including ISO 20022 and Swift SR2026 requirements.
• Connected customer experience: Provides corporate clients with a single channel to initiate requests, collaborate securely, approve transactions, and track progress in real time, enhancing visibility, control, and operational efficiency while maintaining governance and oversight.
• Foundation for future growth: Built on an open and scalable architecture, the platform supports BRAC Bank’s long-term digital transformation strategy and provides flexibility to expand capabilities, support growing transaction volumes and adopt new technologies as business needs evolve.
Executive Perspective: Modernizing Trade for Growth
“This implementation marks an important milestone in our trade finance transformation. By digitizing and streamlining trade operations, we are enhancing transparency, control and efficiency across the trade finance lifecycle, enabling us to serve our corporate clients with greater speed and reliability. This advanced trade solutions brings us closer to our ambition of becoming the most preferred trade bank in Bangladesh by consistently delivering superior value to our customers,” said Tareq Refat Ullah Khan, Managing Director & CEO at BRAC Bank PLC.
"As trade finance continues to play a vital role in supporting businesses and economic growth, banks are seeking technology that simplifies operations while delivering a better customer experience,” said Andrew Bateman, EVP for Lending at Finastra. “We’re delighted to support BRAC Bank on its transformation journey. Through our front-to-back trade finance capabilities, the bank has established a modern and scalable platform that increases operational efficiency, enhances visibility across the trade lifecycle, and delivers a more connected experience for its corporate customers.”
The go-live marks another milestone in the relationship between BRAC Bank and Finastra, reflecting a shared commitment to modernizing trade finance operations, and helping businesses benefit from more efficient, transparent, and digitally enabled trade services.

title: Money20/20 Reveals the Winners of the 2026 Money Awards, Honoring Global Leaders Shaping the Future of Money
summary:
Money20/20, the world's leading fintech show and the place where money does business, today announced the winners of the 2026 Money Awards following a live awards ceremony held yesterday evening at Money20/20 USA in Las Vegas. Recognizing the companies, products, partnerships and the leaders transforming financial services, the awards celebrate innovators setting new standards across the global money ecosystem.
Now in its second year, The Money Awards have been established as a global benchmark for excellence across fintech, banking, payments and financial innovation. This year's winners were selected from a highly competitive field of entries from across the world and represent some of the most impactful and forward-thinking organizations shaping the future of money, from breakthrough startups and fast-growing fintechs to established financial institutions and industry-defining partnerships.
The winners were revealed on October 18 before an audience of industry leaders, investors, innovators, and decision makers, recognizing the achievements, ideas and collaborations driving the next chapter of financial services and the future of money.
Grania Chesterton, VP, Awards at Money20/20, said: "The Money Awards celebrate the very best of global fintech, recognizing the companies and innovations setting new standards for our industry. This year's winners span 8 countries across 4 continents, with work from Bangladesh, Colombia, Cyprus, Pakistan, Singapore, South Korea, UK and USA. They have each demonstrated exceptional ambition, innovation and real-world impact, earning their place among the industry's best in class. Congratulations to every winner on this well-deserved recognition. This is their moment to shine."
The 2026 Money Awards winners were recognized across the following categories:
DIAMOND
BOLTTECH – Grand Prix
YELLOW CARD – Gold Money Award
BKASH LIMITED – Silver Money Award
OPEN REWARDS INC – Bronze Money Award
Mary Ellen Iskenderian, President & CEO, Women's World Banking, said: "What distinguished Bolttech and Yellow Card, the Diamond jury's Grand Prix and Gold winners, was their ability to pair global scale with inclusion. Bolttech is pushing innovation at scale in insurtech, including accessible protection products, in a sector that has not kept pace with payments and other financial services. Yellow Card is building the digital infrastructure across the Global South that can help turn the promise of stablecoins into genuinely broader financial access."
EARLY STAGE STARTUP
CHARM SECURITY – Grand Prix
SOCRATIX AI – Silver Money Award
GROWTH STAGE STARTUP
TRACE FINANCE – Grand Prix

Bernardo Brites, Rafael Luz and Leone Parise built Trace Finance to bridge that gap, scaling past $10 billion in volume in just a few years. They proved to our jury that the next fintech giants won't just build a faster rail. They'll orchestrate a fragmented world of rails to work smarter and more seamlessly as one."
BANKING
OMNISIENT - Grand Prix
TRUE LINK – Gold Money Award
DRIVEWEALTH – Silver Money Award
JAZZCASH, A VEON GROUP FINTECH -Silver Money Award
GRADIENT LABS - Bronze Money Award
HTS (HOPPER TECHNOLOGY SOLUTIONS) - Bronze Money Award

SARDINE - Bronze Money Award

As we explore new frontiers and rapid innovation in technology and AI, its a good reminder to continue to expand financial reach by harnessing new sources beyond the traditional frameworks. The use of non-traditional data is innovative, addresses a meaningful societal problem and demonstrates measurable impact.”

PRIVY, A STRIPE COMPANY – Grand Prix
BKASH LIMITED – Gold Money Award

They took on the challenge of simplifying complex infrastructure for companies of all sizes, across industries, and executed exceptionally well. The result is that their customers can now go global without the burden of building for each market one by one. This is innovation with purpose, delivered at scale."

title: VIVA Finance Secures $150 Million Credit Facility With Viola Credit to Accelerate Growth and Expand Access to Fair Financial Products
summary:
VIVA Finance, an Atlanta-based financial technology platform specializing in accessible, payroll-linked consumer credit solutions, today announced that it has closed a $150 million credit facility with Viola Credit, a leading global alternative asset manager focusing on technology-enabled lending.
The new facility will provide VIVA Finance with significant capital to accelerate the growth of its core lending operations. By leveraging its proprietary payroll-linked repayment infrastructure, VIVA delivers transparent, affordable personal loans to everyday consumers who are often underserved by traditional credit bureaus and legacy banking institutions.
"This strategic partnership with Viola Credit represents a major milestone for VIVA as we continue to scale our platform and expand our market footprint," said Jack Markwalter, CEO and founder of VIVA Finance. "Viola Credit’s deep expertise in fintech and structured finance makes them an ideal partner for this next phase of our growth. This debt facility empowers us to bring our responsible credit solutions to even more consumers, helping them achieve financial stability and avoid predatory alternatives."
VIVA Finance’s platform integrates directly with employees’ direct deposit, enabling seamless, low-risk repayments that allow the Company to offer better terms and lower interest rates than traditional personal loan alternatives. The demand for responsible, payroll-linked loans continues to surge as employees struggle to access affordable credit products during times of financial emergency.
"VIVA Finance has built an exceptional platform that addresses a critical gap in consumer finance," said Michael Chen, Managing Director, Head of US Investments at Viola Credit. "Their innovative approach to payroll integration and commitment to responsible lending have driven impressive performance. We are thrilled to partner with Jack, Hodges and the entire VIVA team to support their continued expansion and mission."
The announcement of the Viola Credit facility builds on a period of rapid momentum for VIVA Finance, which has continued to expand its distribution footprint through strategic partnerships across the employee credit ecosystem.

title: Visa, BILL and Billtrust Launch First Live Pilot for Trusted AI Agent Payments Between Buyer and Supplier Platforms
summary:
Visa and Billtrust today announced they have launched the first live pilot to enable trusted AI agents to initiate and complete approved buyer invoice payments end-to-end through supplier portals.
Until now, many payment portals relied on human authentication requirements that limited how approved payments could be automated. Together, with leading accounts payable and receivable solutions providers BILL and Billtrust, the Visa Intelligent CommerceTM portfolio helps bridge that gap. Leveraging offerings such as Visa Trusted Agent Protocol, AI agents can now be securely authenticated to credentialed portals. As a result, buyer payments that previously relied on manual entry can be completed by trusted AI agents, while preserving supplier control and oversight.
How trusted AI agents are overcoming one of payment automation’s biggest barriers
The flow begins when the authorized BILL Payment Agent — registered using Visa’s Trusted Agent Protocol and Agentic Directory — uses tokenized payment credentials and controls aligned with the buyer’s approved payment instructions to issue payments on behalf of BILL's customers. Supported by capabilities within the Visa Intelligent Commerce (VIC) portfolio, this enables BILL to securely automate card payments for supplier invoices.
Once the payment is initiated, Billtrust leverages Visa's Trusted Agent Protocol to recognize, authenticate, and grant access to the authorized agent enabling BILL to complete the invoice payment on the customer's behalf. This agent authentication can satisfy the site protections historically provided by CAPTCHA and other bot blocking mechanisms, without requiring an additional agent login. As a result, Billtrust customers can receive fast portal payments in accordance with their acceptance policy, which can help accelerate cash flow.
“Businesses should not have to choose between automation and control when making payments,” said Mark Nelsen, SVP and Head of Product, Commercial & Money Movement Solutions, Visa. “This pilot applies agentic commerce to a real B2B-payment problem, by having trusted agents complete payments across platforms. Working with BILL and Billtrust, we are testing how identity, payment controls and transaction visibility can make that model work.”
Building trust into agent-initiated B2B payments
Drawing on capabilities within the Visa Intelligent Commerce portfolio, including Visa's Trusted Agent Protocol, the pilot enables:
A recognized and authenticated AI agent acting on behalf of an identified buyer
Tokenized payment credentials rather than shared supplier-portal logins
Payment controls tied to the customer’s approved payment instruction
A purpose-built payment path tied to the specific invoice
Visibility into the authorization and completion of the payment
"Nearly 500,000 businesses trust BILL to move, manage and maximize their money, and that trust depends on removing friction without sacrificing accuracy and security of supplier payments. For too long, supplier portals have been friction points, requiring a person to manually complete what should be an automated step,” said Archana Prasad, SVP of Payments and Financial Services at BILL. “With Visa and Billtrust, BILL’s AI-powered payments technology is closing that gap: the payment gets done, the supplier gets paid faster, and finance teams get their time back."
For suppliers using Billtrust, the pilot creates a way to recognize and accept payments initiated by trusted business agents, helping release trapped cash while retaining the information needed to process and reconcile the payment within their existing payment acceptance policy. For buyers using BILL, automating this last manual step can give finance teams back the time they'd spend manually keying information into supplier payment portals.
“Agentic commerce will only move forward if businesses can trust agents to operate across systems with the same clarity and accountability they expect from people,” said Kunal Patel, SVP Payments, Billtrust. “By connecting buyer-side invoice approval with supplier-side payment acceptance, this pilot shows how authorized agents can complete business transactions, releasing trapped cash faster while adhering to a complex acceptance policy and preserving visibility and control for both sides.”

title: WEX Survey Reveals 85% of Businesses Face Internal Obstacles to B2B Payment Modernisation
summary:
Organizations are expanding their use of digital payments, but internal barriers continue to complicate modernization, according to a new survey from WEX, a global leader in intelligent payment solutions. Nearly two-thirds increased their use of digital payments over the past year, while 85% report internal obstacles such as implementation costs, integration challenges, and change management hurdles. The findings appear in WEX’s new report, “Modernization of B2B Payment: An Evolution Is Underway.”
While over 80% of organizations acknowledge that payments drive overall business value, a significant execution gap remains. Even so, a clear path forward is emerging, as 94% of organizations are using or planning to adopt AI across their payment lifecycle.
“Financial leaders understand that payments drive organizational value, both as a revenue generator and a strategic growth lever, but having the tools to realize that potential remains a major hurdle,” said Eric Frankovic, President of Corporate Payments at WEX. “Today’s most innovative leaders recognize the question facing their organization is no longer whether to modernize, but how fast they can get there.”
The Problems: Fragmentation, Barriers to Change
As transaction volume grows, manual payment processes can no longer keep up with the workload. Over half of surveyed organizations (56%) now handle more than 1,000 supplier payments monthly, totaling millions in spend. Yet most continue to rely on fragmented traditional methods – managing payments across multiple bank portals and card platforms. For 74% of leaders, juggling these disconnected vendors creates a heavy administrative burden.
However, system fragmentation is only part of the challenge. WEX’s research reveals that 85% of organizations face internal barriers to change, driven by technology implementation costs (51%), integration challenges with existing software (41%), and change management hurdles (38%). Alongside these operational obstacles, 54% of leaders also cite security concerns as a major barrier. With fraud impacting over a quarter of surveyed organizations in the past six months alone, fears surrounding data privacy breaches and payment interception keep many finance teams anchored to familiar, legacy processes.
The Solutions: Digital Infrastructure, Automation
Despite these hurdles with financial infrastructure, WEX’s research reveals that forward-looking organizations are not waiting for legacy friction to resolve itself – they are actively reshaping payment strategies to gain a competitive edge. Nearly two-thirds of organizations increased their use of digital payments over the past year, with finance leaders turning to modern tools to reduce costs (53%), streamline daily workflows (51%), and strengthen security controls (47%).
Automation and artificial intelligence also serve as critical engines driving this shift, with 94% of organizations using or planning to adopt AI across the payment lifecycle. Rather than replacing human oversight, finance teams are deploying AI to solve immediate operational pain points, focusing primarily on fraud detection and risk scoring (64%), invoice processing and reconciliation (51%), and predictive cash flow forecasting (43%). Looking ahead, 44% of organizations plan to adopt agentic AI within the next two years to automate complex, multi-step workflows, transforming payments into a proactive financial growth lever.

title: Mercury Launches AI-Native Payroll
summary:
Mercury, the technology company providing radically different banking* for over 450,000 customers, today launched Mercury Payroll, bringing payroll directly into the Mercury experience. Mercury Payroll lets founders pay employees and contractors and offer benefits from the same account they already use to manage their money, with AI-powered capabilities through Mercury Command that help simplify payroll tasks and reduce administrative work. Mercury Payroll also handles tax and payroll compliance needs so that founders can focus their time on what matters most: building their business.
“Hiring your first employee is one of the biggest moments in building a company, but what comes immediately after, like setting up payroll, taxes, benefits, and compliance is far more complicated than it needs to be,” said Immad Akhund, co-founder and CEO of Mercury. “In 2026 with AI we can make what was toil for entrepreneurs as easy as a quick chat. We’re launching Mercury Payroll so paying your team can feel as simple as moving money in Mercury.”
Payroll is one of the largest recurring transactions a business makes, yet it has historically existed separately from the account where a company manages its money, requiring founders to onboard to another provider, connect banking information, configure tax and state registrations, and reconcile activity across systems. Mercury Payroll brings payroll alongside the money that powers it, giving founders a direct path between hiring someone and paying them.
Mercury Payroll joins banking, cards, spend management, invoicing, bill pay, accounting, and Mercury Command, Mercury’s AI agent, giving founders a complete view of their company’s finances in one place. Command works across all of it, so founders can analyze their full financial picture and take actions through simple natural-language requests.
With Mercury Payroll, customers can:
Get set up quickly: Mercury already has existing customers’ EINs and entity details on file, so they can set up their first payroll run in under 15 minutes. New hires onboard themselves, entering their own tax forms and direct deposit details.
Pay employees and contractors: Run W-2 employee payroll, pay 1099 contractors in the U.S., and issue bonuses and other one-time payments directly from a Mercury account.
Simplify payroll tasks with AI: Use Mercury's AI agent, Command, to help with payroll tasks like updating an employee's salary, adding overtime hours to a pay run, adding recurring reimbursements, deductions or earnings to an employee, issuing bonuses, and more.
Hand off payroll tax and compliance: Mercury Payroll files and remits federal and state payroll taxes, handles W-2s and 1099s at year-end, handles unemployment claims, and reviews state agency correspondence. Mercury’s in-house team registers companies in new states as they hire, with coverage in all 50 states.
Offer benefits: Access health insurance, 401(k) options through Human Interest or a self-managed plan, and HSA, FSA, ICHRA, and commuter benefits.

title: Moneyhub and Know Your Dosh Bring Open Banking to Family Financial Planning
summary:
Moneyhub, the leading Applied AI and data intelligence platform for financial institutions, today announced that Know Your Dosh, a UK family financial management app, has selected its technology. The partnership will let Know Your Dosh users automatically sync accounts across a household, including current accounts, savings, investments and pensions. This gives families a single, shared view of their finances without the friction of manual updates or the risk of sharing login credentials. Once connected, a full insights suite is unlocked, including a feature that details a families’ true household budget. 
Know Your Dosh is built around a simple truth.  Financial transparency within a family is rare, financial admin is a headache, and money conversations can feel even harder.  It is designed for households managing shared financial lives across different accounts, life stages, and generations, and since going live with Moneyhub tracks more than £200 million in assets through its dashboard. Until now, keeping track of those assets has required manual input. A barrier that stops many families from engaging with their finances altogether.  
By integrating Moneyhub's FCA-regulated infrastructure, Know Your Dosh removes that barrier entirely. Accounts update automatically through direct, secure connections. No manual reconciliation is required. Families can instead focus on  what they have, what they owe, and what they are planning for. 
The platform allows users to set granular controls over what each family member can see, so a household can share a consolidated financial picture without every individual having full visibility of every account. A partner can track joint finances without accessing the other's personal savings, or a parent can oversee household budgets without a teenager seeing the full picture. 
The partnership arrives at a moment of growing urgency around household financial visibility, with the total value of dormant and forgotten assets held by UK families estimated to be at £89 billion. Moneyhub's data aggregation capability is designed to address precisely this problem, ensuring nothing important gets lost, and no account falls silently out of sight. 
Dan Scholey, CPO at Moneyhub, said: "Most fintech is built for the individual, but with modern, secure data sharing we can unlock those relationships that matter. The team at Know Your Dosh have built something that meets families where they actually are. Moneyhub’s job is to make sure the data behind it is as complete and as accurate as possible.”    
Varun Aggarwal, Founder and CEO at Know Your Dosh, said: "When I lost my father, the financial chaos that followed wasn’t because my family was careless, but because no one had ever created a space for us to understand our money together. That experience is why Know Your Dosh exists. We built it for every family that avoids the money conversation because it feels too complicated to start. Partnering with Moneyhub means our users no longer have to do the hard work of keeping their finances up to date. It happens automatically, securely, and in the background. And crucially, every family member sees exactly what they need to see, and nothing they don’t. The UK has the infrastructure to make this work at scale, and we’re excited to build here first.”

title: Probly Wraps Up TOKEN2049 Singapore and WHALE3RA, Strengthening Its Presence in On-Chain Prediction Markets
summary: The British Virgin Islands, Road Town, October 2026 — Probly, an on-chain prediction market for sports, politics, crypto, finance, and global events, has concluded its participation as a Gold Sponsor of TOKEN2049 Singapore and co-host of the WHALE3RA Afterparty alongside BloFin, TxFlow, and other ecosystem partners.   Across TOKEN2049 week, Probly connected with traders, builders, infrastructure teams, partners, and Web3 communities around the growing role of prediction markets as a way to express views on real-world events. The week also gave Probly an opportunity to introduce its approach to prediction markets to a broader crypto-native audience: simple access, broad market coverage, self-custody USDC, peer-to-peer trading, and verifiable on-chain settlement. From Market Opinions to On-Chain Signals Prediction markets are increasingly becoming an interface for turning expectations about future events into market signals. For Probly, TOKEN2049 provided an opportunity to bring that idea directly to an audience already accustomed to trading changing market conditions, information, and expectations. The name Probly comes from “probably,” the word people use when the outcome of an event remains uncertain. It is also inspired by P(A), the mathematical notation used to represent the probability of an event.   Probly currently supports 5,100 events and 47,000 markets across Sports, Geopolitics, Crypto, Finance, Economy, and Politics. The platform also offers 172 active live markets for same-day trading, including high-frequency Crypto “Up or Down” rolling markets across BTC, ETH, SOL, and XRP. Probly is the first prediction market application developed through TxFlow Improvement Protocol 3 (TIP3). Settlement through TxFlow enables on-chain settlement, automatic USDC payouts, and no manual claim step. Bringing the Prediction Market Conversation to WHALE3RA Probly also co-hosted WHALE3RA at MARQUEE Singapore during TOKEN2049 week alongside BloFin, TxFlow, and other ecosystem partners.   The event brought together traders, builders, funds, exchanges, infrastructure teams, and Web3 communities, giving Probly an opportunity to engage directly with many of the audiences shaping the next generation of crypto products.   For Probly, these conversations reinforced an important direction for the product: prediction markets should not be limited to occasional major events. They can become a more active interface for following changing information, forming a view, and trading expectations as events develop. What Comes Next for Probly Following TOKEN2049 Singapore, Probly will continue developing its prediction market experience around accessibility, broader event coverage, frequent trading opportunities, and transparent on-chain infrastructure. The company will also continue working with ecosystem and infrastructure partners as it develops new ways for users to express views on future outcomes through on-chain markets.   TOKEN2049 and WHALE3RA marked another step in bringing Probly’s core idea to a wider audience: uncertainty is everywhere, and markets can make collective expectations around what happens next more visible, transparent, and useful. Before It Happens. About Probly Probly is a prediction market built on TxFlow L1 through TxFlow Improvement Protocol 3 (TIP3). It turns views about future events into continuously updated market signals across sports, crypto, economics, news, culture, weather, and other real-world categories.   Probly combines real-time markets, broad event coverage, fully on-chain settlement, and self-custodied USDC infrastructure. Its mission is to make collective expectations more immediate, transparent, and useful by converting uncertainty into a price. title: Supermicro Brings NVIDIA Aerial RAN Computer Solutions to the Network Edge With Nokia to Enable Low-Latency AI Services
summary:
Super Micro Computer, Inc., an AI, Enterprise, Storage, and 5G/Edge Total IT Solution Provider featuring Data Center Building Block Solutions® (DCBBS), is now working with Nokia to deploy Artificial Intelligence-Radio Access Networks (AI-RAN) from distributed cell sites to centralized network hubs. The solution combines Nokia's RAN technology and network expertise with the NVIDIA Aerial RAN Computer platform, supported by Supermicro's AI-optimized infrastructure. By bringing accelerated compute closer to the access network, it enables radio and AI workloads to run on shared infrastructure, supporting applications which require proximity and predictable service levels-including voice AI, vision AI, physical AI, and internal uses such as autonomous network operations.
"AI-RAN is redefining networks for AI, turning mobile infrastructure into a shared foundation for connectivity, AI for RAN, AI on RAN, and broader distributed AI services," says Charles Liang, president and CEO, Supermicro. "Together with Nokia and NVIDIA, we are bringing accelerated computing to every layer of the network, enabling operators to maximize infrastructure efficiency, deploy new AI services, and prepare for AI-native 6G. Our DCBBS approach delivers the flexibility and performance to accelerate deployment and turn network infrastructure into a platform for innovation." For more information on the latest AI-RAN solutions, click here.
Embedding accelerated compute into the RAN enables operators to run network and AI workloads on the same infrastructure, improving spectral efficiency, automating network operations, and optimizing energy use while creating new opportunities for edge AI services. Combining Supermicro systems with Nokia's RAN technology and software, the NVIDIA Aerial RAN Computer platform provides modular, right-sized CPU and GPU configurations for deployment from cell sites to MSO and aggregation locations, with NVIDIA ConnectX technology providing high-speed, software-defined networking. Together, these capabilities give operators a flexible foundation for low-latency AI applications today and a software-driven evolution path towards 6G networks.
"AI-RAN represents an important step towards more intelligent and adaptable mobile networks," said Emma Falck, President of Mobile Infrastructure at Nokia. "By combining Nokia's leadership in radio networks with NVIDIA accelerated computing and Supermicro's flexible infrastructure, we are giving operators a practical way to bring RAN and AI workloads together across their networks. This will help operators improve network performance and automation today while creating a foundation for new edge AI services and AI-native 6G."
"AI-RAN brings together networking, accelerated computing, and intelligence to help operators make better use of their infrastructure while opening new opportunities for edge AI services," said Soma Velayutham, VP of Telecoms, NVIDIA. "Nokia and Supermicro are helping operators deploy NVIDIA Aerial RAN Computer solutions across diverse network environments, from distributed cell sites to centralized RAN locations, with the flexibility to scale intelligence capabilities as demand grows."
Supermicro's modular, right-sized systems for NVIDIA ARC span distributed cell sites, aggregation locations, and core hubs, enabling operators to precisely deploy AI capacity where it is needed.
Distributed cell sites: The ARC MGX 2U Short-depth platform brings inference closer to radios, users, and applications. NVIDIA MGX is a modular reference architecture for accelerated computing, helping system builders design future-compatible systems faster, reducing costs, accelerating time to market, and improving ROI. Supermicro's dual-node ARC-Pro combines an NVIDIA Grace C1 CPU and NVIDIA RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell Server Edition GPU per node in a 429 mm chassis, delivering up to 1.6 PFLOPS of FP4 AI performance. For edge networking functions such as Service Management and Orchestration, the ARC-Compact delivers high efficiency compute performance in a 1U, short-depth form factor.
Centralized MSO and aggregation sites: The ARC MGX 2U supports higher-throughput, coordinated inference. This system class comes with a choice between dual NVIDIA Vera CPUs or dual x86 processors and two NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs. These systems support multi-cell workloads, including coordinated scheduling and beamforming, as well as voice, vision, and physical AI.
Core network hubs: The ARC MGX 4U provides high-density, air-cooled inference with up to eight NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs. Supermicro's 4U AI servers deliver dual x86 CPUs and up to 6 TB of DDR5 memory to support large-scale inference and model update workloads. This configuration comes with the option for an NVIDIA ConnectX-8 switchboard, providing PCIe Gen 6 for even faster GPU-GPU interconnectivity.
Supermicro's servers for NVIDIA ARC are generally available now. The ARC MGX 2U with dual Vera processor is on display on Supermicro's booth at NVIDIA GTC Berlin, October 20–22, 2026, and will be available later this year. The 2U ARC-Pro is planned for customer testing later this year, with general availability in the first half of 2027.

title: PPRO Launches Local Payments Council for Agentic Commerce
summary:
PPRO has today launched the Local Payments Council for Agentic Commerce alongside founding members BLIK, EPI, Bancontact Company, and DIAS, with other payment schemes committed to joining. The new industry initiative brings the local payments community together to align the rapidly developing agentic commerce ecosystem with how consumers prefer to pay across global markets.
Agentic commerce is moving quickly from concept to reality, and the payments infrastructure underpinning it is still developing. Global card networks have introduced frameworks designed to enable trusted agent-led transactions. However, questions remain around how preferred local payment options will function when AI agents perform purchases rather than human shoppers.
The Local Payments Council for Agentic Commerce brings together payment schemes and relevant industry participants to shape the technical standards defining how local payment methods integrate into agentic protocols.
Alexander Matthey, CTO at PPRO, said: “For agentic commerce to continue gaining momentum, consumers need to be able to use the local payment methods they already know and trust, even if an AI agent is purchasing on their behalf. This next phase of development needs to make sure the rules around how local payments work with agentic protocols are there from the outset, rather than treated as an additional layer later on. We are bringing payment schemes together to find practical solutions to technical challenges and ensure local payments play a key role in the development of agentic commerce.”
The council aims to focus on five key areas:
Out-of-band authorisation and session hand-off
Agent identity and attestation for non-card rails
Consent, mandates, and delegated authority
Disputes, refunds, and liability
Discoverability and agent-surface eligibility
With AI-referred shoppers converting nearly 50% more and recording 14% higher average order values than shoppers arriving from organic search, the council aims to ensure local payment methods are ready to work with AI platforms as commerce increasingly shifts to AI-driven experiences.

Laura Bowden, Chief Financial Officer at McLaren Racing, said: “Partnering closely with Airwallex demonstrates our long-term commitment to investing in faster, more efficient technology. Airwallex is our first Official AI Finance Partner and we’re confident in their ability to help us run our financial operations faster and more efficiently.”
Pranav Sood, Chief Financial Officer at Airwallex, added: “Formula 1 is built on the pursuit of marginal gains, and that mindset has shaped our partnership with McLaren Racing. Over the past three seasons, we’ve shown how smarter financial infrastructure and AI-native technology can help global organisations move faster and operate with greater control across borders. As we become an Official AI Finance Partner of the McLaren Mastercard Formula 1 Team from 2027, we’re proud to support their business growth and deepen our relationship. This closely aligns with our broader strategy to help businesses move faster and more profitably than their competitors, and as we enter the Agentic Banking era, we’re focused on deploying intelligent AI capabilities across our unified stack with Agentic Business Accounts at the center.”
Airwallex will continue to provide technology that supports McLaren’s digital partner merchandise platform, enabling the collection of payments from customers using a range of global and local payment methods.
This news follows three successful Formula 1 seasons of the partnership, through which Airwallex has supported McLaren’s global financial operations as it secured its 10th Constructors’ World Championship and as Lando Norris won the Drivers’ Championship in 2025. Last season also represented the sport’s highest TV viewing figures in five years, attracting a total cumulative audience of 1.83 billion, according to Nielsen - up almost 7% on 2024.
Airwallex’s global sports partnership presence continues to move from strength to strength, becoming the Official Finance Software Partner for Arsenal Football Club in July 2025, supporting the club's global financial operations, and both the Official Jersey Patch Partner of the San Francisco Giants and the Official Business Finance Partner of New Zealand’s Super Rugby Club, the Blues, in February 2026.

At Griffin, David will work closely with CEO and co-founder David Jarvis and the executive team to scale the bank and strengthen its financial foundations.

title: Just 9% of Multinationals Fully Complete Companies House ID Checks
summary:
Multinational businesses with UK entities risk falling short on Companies House identity verification and have significant gaps still to close as the 12-month transition period nears its end, according to new research from Vistra, a leading provider of essential business services.
Vistra surveyed 300 directors at multinational businesses with a UK presence, including 50 UK-based directors. While 84% said their organisation was prepared for the new identity verification requirements, the average proportion of relevant directors and persons with significant control (PSCs) who had completed verification stood at just 61%, and only 9% reported full completion.
The findings come as the 12-month transition period, which began when mandatory identity verification was introduced on 18 November 2025, nears its end. Existing directors must provide their personal code with their company’s next confirmation statement, while existing PSCs have individual verification periods based on their circumstances. The research also follows the first court action for identity verification offences, with three directors fined in September following prosecutions brought by the Insolvency Service.
Many businesses have also yet to complete some of the key practical steps required for verification, with only 26% saying they had checked that Companies House records for directors and PSCs were accurate. Meanwhile, just 20% had identified all directors and PSCs requiring verification and 22% had obtained and recorded the necessary Companies House personal codes.
The picture is particularly pronounced among UK-based respondents. While 86% said their organisation was prepared, none said all relevant directors and PSCs had completed verification. On average, UK respondents estimated that 60% had completed the process, with only 14% at least three-quarters of the way through.
Cross-border structures are adding to the challenge, with more than three-quarters (76%) saying verifying directors and PSCs based outside the UK had created additional compliance complexity. Among respondents with directors or PSCs based outside the UK, coordinating people across different jurisdictions and time zones was the most commonly cited barrier (27%), followed by differences in identity documentation and data protection or information-sharing concerns (both 24%).
The process is also uncovering issues in the corporate information businesses hold. Almost three in ten respondents found discrepancies between Companies House and internal records (30%), missing supporting documentation (29%), out-of-date director information (29%) or incorrect or incomplete PSC and ownership information (29%). Only 1% said their review had uncovered no issues.
The wider ECCTA reforms are also adding to the time businesses spend managing their UK entities. Two-thirds (66%) of respondents said recent corporate transparency, identity verification and corporate liability requirements had added at least 10 working hours a month, with an average increase of 13.9 hours. Among UK-based respondents, the average rises to 17.3 hours a month, equivalent to almost 26 eight-hour working days a year.
Meg Ogunsola, Global Head of Entity Management at Vistra, commented: “There is a clear gap between how prepared businesses feel and how much of the practical work has actually been completed. For multinationals, this challenge is magnified by having directors, PSCs and corporate information spread across multiple jurisdictions.
“These reforms are an important step towards improving corporate transparency, but they are also creating additional work for businesses. The findings show why having accurate entity data, clear ownership of the process and visibility over individual verification requirements is so important. As the transition period nears its end, businesses should be clear on who still needs to verify, their individual due dates and whether the information supporting that process is accurate and complete.”
The research also found significant differences in preparedness and implementation between markets:
US: Reported the highest preparedness at 94%, despite having the lowest average completion level at 55%.
EU: Reported the highest average completion level at 73%, with 34% saying all relevant directors and PSCs had completed verification.
Middle East: Reported the greatest cross-border complexity, with 88% saying verification of directors and PSCs based outside the UK had created additional compliance complexity.
APAC: Recorded the lowest preparedness at 72%.
UK: Reported the highest additional administrative impact, at an average of 17.3 hours a month.

title: Why centralized exchanges refuse to list legacy crypto tokens without explicit SEC immunity
summary: Vault12 raised $17.45 million selling VGT in 2018 and says it met or dropped every promise, yet the token has never traded on a centralized exchange.
content: Centralized cryptocurrency exchanges are increasingly reluctant to list legacy digital tokens unless they receive explicit immunity from the SEC. Despite raising millions and fulfilling its commitments, the 2018 project Vault12 and its VGT token have struggled to secure listings on major centralized trading platforms amid ongoing regulatory uncertainty.
content_ta: SEC-யிடம் இருந்து வெளிப்படையான பாதுகாப்பு ஒப்புதல் கிடைத்தால் மட்டுமே பழைய கிரிப்டோ டோக்கன்களை பட்டியலிட முடியும் என்பதில் சென்ட்ரல் எக்ஸ்சேஞ்சுகள் உறுதியாக உள்ளன. பல மில்லியன் டாலர்களை திரட்டி தனது வாக்குறுதிகளை நிறைவேற்றிய போதிலும், Vault12 மற்றும் அதன் VGT டோக்கன் போன்ற திட்டங்கள் முக்கிய எக்ஸ்சேஞ்சுகளில் பட்டியலிடப்படுவதில் தொடர்ந்து சிரமங்களை எதிர்கொண்டு வருகின்றன.

title: Anza’s Alpenglow goes live on Solana, cutting finality to 150 milliseconds
summary: Solana activated Alpenglow, replacing TowerBFT and cutting transaction finality from 12.8 seconds to about 150 milliseconds.
content: Solana has activated Anza’s Alpenglow, replacing the previous TowerBFT consensus mechanism. This significant upgrade successfully reduces transaction finality from 12.8 seconds down to approximately 150 milliseconds, dramatically improving network speed and performance for users and developers alike.
content_ta: Solana நெட்வொர்க் Anza-வின் Alpenglow-வை இயக்கியுள்ளது, இது முந்தைய TowerBFT முறைக்கு பதிலாக செயல்படுகிறது. இந்த முக்கிய மேம்பாடு பரிவர்த்தனை இறுதி நேரத்தை 12.8 வினாடிகளிலிருந்து சுமார் 150milliseconds ஆக வெற்றிகரமாக குறைத்துள்ளது, இது நெட்வொர்க்கின் வேகத்தை குறிப்பிடத்தக்க அளவில் மேம்படுத்துகிறது.

title: Crypto rallies point to slower USDC growth and faster USDT growth, study finds
summary:

title: The Started Advisory Board Brings FinTech Leaders Together for Candid AI Debate
summary:
As excitement and concern around AI grow in equal measure, the Started Advisory Board convened CEOs, founders and financial services leaders for a behind-closed-doors discussion on accountability, trust and what the sector cannot afford to get wrong.
On Thursday 15 October, the Started Advisory Board, a unique fintech communications-focused think tank, brought together senior leaders from fintech, banking, payments, investment and media for an open debate on AI, accountability and trust in financial services. 
Curated by Started PR, and hosted by Checkout.com, An Evening with the Started Advisory Board explored how financial services businesses can realise AI’s benefits while retaining human judgement, clear accountability and customer trust. An audience open mic invited guests to challenge the panel, share experiences and question assumptions about how AI will shape the sector. 
The evening opened with remarks from Asif Faruque, Senior Director of Communications at Checkout.com, before a live debate hosted by author and presenter Ian Horne. Contributors included Advisory Board members Susanne Chishti, Katie Ramsey, Jas Shah, Raf De Kimpe, Jason Williams and David Savage. The event brought together a high-calibre audience of CEOs, founders, operators and those building the next generation of financial services in the age of AI. 
The debate explored the gap between AI’s promise and its practical value, the balance between innovation and accountability, and the implications for jobs, skills and customer trust. Panellists and audience members questioned whether faster output means better outcomes, where human judgement must remain central and how businesses can encourage experimentation while managing risk. 
Fintech Product Consultant Jas Shah said: “The perception of how much AI is transforming financial institutions is far from the reality. I think people are talking more about what they’re doing with AI than actually doing it. The human element is still very important: understanding the processes, understanding the value your company offers and feeding that into a process AI can use to create value.” 
The conversation also explored the tension between encouraging experimentation and controlling “shadow AI”, where employees use tools outside approved systems. Contributors called for clear, regularly reviewed policies, effective tools and a culture where employees can learn without fear of failure. They also questioned whether restrictive policies push experimentation out of sight, increasing risks around confidential data and oversight. 
Founder and Chair of FINTECH Circle Susanne Chishti said: “It’s a fine balance. You want everybody to use AI as much as possible, but within guardrails, especially in a regulated financial services company. Having humans in control is very important but they can become the bottleneck. As AI enabled work is faster to produce, it creates more work to check it. Working with AI is powerful and fun, but it doesn’t necessarily give you the free time you initially expected as you find new AI applications which you want to pursue to get things done.”
The evening highlighted the continuing value of distinctive expertise, personal relationships and face-to-face discussion. Contributors argued that credibility and trust will become more valuable as AI makes content and other outputs easier to produce, placing greater importance on original perspectives, strong networks and the exchange of ideas in person. 
The Started Advisory Board brings together founders, investors, operators and industry commentators to inform Started PR’s work and give clients access to expertise and relationships across financial services. Its members are David M. Brear, Jason Mikula, Sarah Kocianski, David Savage, Jas Shah, Jason Williams, Monica Millares, Raf De Kimpe, Susanne Chishti and Katie Ramsey. 
Kimberley Waldron, Chair of the Started Advisory Board and Managing Director of Started PR, said: “Our Advisory Board and wider network brought real experience and challenge to this important industry debate. As our panel discussed, AI is creating huge opportunities, but human judgement, accountability and trust remain essential. Thank you to Checkout.com for hosting a candid conversation about what financial services needs to get right.”

title: TreviPay Expands Pay by Invoice Availability for Walmart Business Customers
summary:
TreviPay, a global B2B payments infrastructure partner, today announced the general availability of Pay By Invoice for eligible Walmart Business customers. Following an initial pilot, the expanded availability gives more organizations a new way to manage purchasing and payments online and in Walmart stores. Walmart Business Pay By Invoice provides net 30-day terms, a dedicated business line of credit and detailed invoicing built into the Walmart Business purchasing experience.
Powered by TreviPay, Walmart Business Pay By Invoice is designed to give organizations greater flexibility in how they manage business purchases and payments. Eligible customers can get what they need and pay on net 30-day terms, helping them preserve cash flow for other priorities while keeping operations moving. Purchasing controls and payment reconciliation also help organizations share purchasing responsibilities while maintaining oversight and keeping purchase activity, invoices, payments, returns and refunds organized in one place.
“Retailers have a significant opportunity to build stronger relationships with business buyers by recognizing that their purchasing needs are different from those of consumers,” said Brandon Spear, CEO of TreviPay. “Business buyers need payment choice, purchasing controls and terms that align with how their organizations manage cash flow. When retailers make those capabilities part of the purchasing experience, they make it easier for business customers to buy from them and come back again and again.”
The general availability follows an initial rollout of the TreviPay-powered solution. During that period, Walmart Business customers reported a 90% customer satisfaction score with the program. The results reinforce the value of giving business customers greater flexibility and control over how they purchase and pay. Pay By Invoice can support organizations with complex purchasing and recordkeeping needs such as:
Schools, colleges and universities can centralize purchasing records across departments or campuses to support budgeting, compliance requirements and audit preparation.
Nonprofits can organize purchasing across programs, events or grant-funded initiatives, while government agencies and public sector organizations can maintain purchasing and payment records to support procurement, financial reporting, compliance and audits.
Businesses can purchase inventory and supplies but enjoy 30 days to pay, thereby preserving cash flow for other expenses, and purchasing controls helping owners and managers share buying responsibilities while maintaining oversight.
